meta.name: Linde India Ltd
meta.about: Linde India Limited, a subsidiary of BOC Group,UK (owns 75% stake in the co), is primarily engaged in manufacture of industrial and medical gases and construction of cryogenic and non cryogenic air separation plants.[1]
meta.keyPoints: Business Segments:[1] a) Gases, Related Products & Services (78% in Q1 FY27 vs 87% in Q1 FY26):[2] The company supplies industrial and specialty gases such as oxygen, nitrogen, and argon through onsite pipeline systems, bulk liquid distribution networks, and packaged gas solutions. Its healthcare portfolio caters to hospitals and healthcare providers by offering medical gases and associated solutions. b) Project Engineering Division (22% in Q1 FY26 vs 13% in Q1 FY26):[3] The company offers turnkey engineering solutions for cryogenic gases, including the design, supply, installation, and commissioning of medium- to large-sized Air Separation Units (ASUs), nitrogen plants, and gas distribution networks. The division also manufactures cryogenic equipment such as distillation columns, cold boxes, cryogenic vessels, and vaporizers for both internal use and external customers.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Linde India (consolidated, Rs crore). Segment model on the two reported segments: Gases & related products (external revenue = segment revenue) and Project Engineering on EXTERNAL revenue only (PED segment revenue less inter-segment plants built for Gases, which are eliminated at cost), so the two sum to reported revenue. Segment margin = segment EBITDA (segment result + segment D&A, AR note 42) as % of segment revenue. Unallocated corporate costs (Screener EBITDA less the sum of segment EBITDA) are a separate line. Treasury income = yield x opening net cash (zero when net debt); other income = recurring non-treasury income plus the LSAS JV share. Valued on P/E, the method the Indian street uses for listed industrial-gas companies.

segments.name: Gases & related products
segments._why: FY26 +4.3% (merchant deliveries +12% to 2,360 TPD; on-site power pass-through fell ~Rs 106 cr, depressing reported revenue). Q1FY27 +9.0%. FY27 +11%: full year of the JSL Jajpur 1,450 tpd ASU and IOCL Panipat N2 plant (capitalised in FY26), the second Tata Steel Kalinganagar 1,800 TPD ASU and the third Dahej ASU (commissioning FY27), merchant growth ~8-10%. FY28 +12%: SAIL Rourkela 1,000 TPD and Electrosteel Bokaro 900 TPD ASUs (under construction at Aug-2026) ramp up. FY29 +10%: steel 6-8% and electronics/solar 18-20% end-market growth (company view) with no new large plant assumed.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 33.7% (FY24), 35.8% (FY25), 40.6% (FY26 incl. the Rs 90 cr reversal; 36.3% without it). Q4FY26 ~36% and Q1FY27 ~35% (PBIT margin 24.3% vs 25.8%: power tariffs, overheads, new-plant depreciation). New on-site plants carry fixed facility fees, so margin rises gently: 35.5% / 36% / 36.5%.

segments.name: Project Engineering (external)
segments._why: External PED revenue: Rs 768 cr (FY24), Rs 445 cr (FY25), Rs 402 cr (FY26); Q1FY27 Rs 150 cr (2.1x Q1FY26). Third-party order book ~Rs 2,000 cr (AGM, Aug-2026) incl. Tata Electronics' Dholera fab and Assam OSAT, Reliance Nagothane ASU, Adani and PSU nitrogen plants. FY27 ~Rs 644 cr (+60%), FY28 ~Rs 740 cr, FY29 ~Rs 703 cr as the current order book is executed; lumpy.
segments._marginWhy: PED PBIT margin on external revenue was 11-14% in CY18-FY24, then 22% (FY25) and 30% (FY26) when inter-segment work for the company's own plants was large (Rs 661 cr and Rs 578 cr) and absorbed overheads; Q1FY27 ~16% EBITDA as external work rose and inter-segment work fell to Rs 75 cr. We assume 16% / 15% / 15%, nearer the long-run level.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Unallocated corporate costs (sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Rs 77 cr (FY24), Rs 70 cr (FY25), Rs 78 cr (FY26): head-office, governance, legal (SEBI/SAT/Supreme Court) and other costs not allocated to segments. Grows ~6% a year.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex Rs 572 cr (FY24), Rs 1,331 cr (FY25), Rs 766 cr (FY26). At Mar-2026: CWIP Rs 1,343 cr, capital commitments Rs 695 cr net of Rs 755 cr of advances already paid. Projects under construction: Tata Kalinganagar second 1,800 TPD ASU, SAIL Rourkela 1,000 TPD, Electrosteel Bokaro 900 TPD, Dahej third ASU, ammonia purification (Gujarat). No guidance; we assume Rs 900 / 750 / 650 cr incl. ~Rs 150 cr a year of maintenance, cylinders and logistics (FY26: Rs 37 cr on special-gas trailers alone).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs 235 cr = 6.2% of average gross block (Rs 3,780 cr). Q1FY27 Rs 62 cr (Rs 250 cr annualised). The engine holds CWIP (Rs 1,343 cr) flat and depreciates capex at once, so we use 6.6% to capture CWIP being capitalised as the Tata, SAIL and Dahej plants start.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied only to positive opening net cash (cash Rs 112 cr + Rs 82 cr investments in renewable SPVs less Rs 79 cr lease liabilities at Mar-2026); with capex above operating cash flow, net cash turns to net debt and this line falls to zero.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Recurring non-treasury other income and the LSAS JV share: FY26 consolidated other income Rs 18 cr plus normal JV share ~Rs 7 cr (excluding the ~Rs 49 cr Bellary Oxygen one-off); Q1FY27 Rs 5.8 cr + Rs 1.6 cr.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest cost (leases and borrowings to fund capex)
assumptions._interestWhy: Rs 13 cr (FY25), Rs 14.5 cr (FY26, incl. Rs 6.2 cr on leases); Q1FY27 Rs 5.9 cr (double Q4FY26). Lease liabilities rose to Rs 79 cr. Capex above operating cash flow after dividends means borrowings of roughly Rs 500-700 cr by FY28 at ~7.5-8%, plus leases.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 consolidated 25.2% (Rs 184.5 cr on Rs 733.5 cr PBT); Q1FY27 25.1%; new regime 25.17% plus deferred tax on the JV.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend held at Rs 12 a share (Rs 102 cr, incl. a special) for FY23-FY26: 19-23% of EPS. We keep roughly Rs 12-13 a share.

dcf._betaWhy: Long-term take-or-pay contracts and a parent-backed balance sheet make cash flows steadier than the market, but merchant pricing, steel and project lumpiness add cyclicality: beta 0.85, cost of equity 11.6%. The engine discounts at the cost of equity; with little debt this is close to WACC.
dcf._tgWhy: Industrial gases grow with industrial output and nominal GDP; 6% nominal, the top of the house 5-6% range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% to 8% by year 15 (India nominal GDP ~10%; gases ~1x industrial growth).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades from ~32% to 32%: gases mix rises but power costs and competition cap it; Linde plc's group EBITDA margin is ~38-40% at global scale.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Gases are capital-heavy (gross block incl. CWIP ~2x sales); growing ~8% needs capex of ~14% of sales (Linde plc spends ~16% of sales).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: All four large ASUs start on time and merchant liquid stays tight: gases grow ~14% a year with EBITDA margin near 38%; PED executes the semiconductor and refinery orders faster at ~18%; the Supreme Court sides with the company and the Praxair matter fades.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Steel capex slows and project start-ups slip a year; INOX, Air Liquide and Air Water add merchant capacity and liquid prices fall; gases grow ~8% with margin ~33.5%; PED orders are delayed and margins fall to ~12%; SEBI acts on the valuation report.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: No broker method for Linde India is public; the Indian street values listed industrial-gas companies on one-year-forward P/E (Motilal Oswal initiated Ellenbarrie at 40x FY27E EPS in Sep-2025). 85x Sep-28E EPS = the stock's 114.5x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (forwardMedian; the Apr-2021 to Mar-2022 points drop out because FY23 was a 15-month year; no trough years), cut by the ~25% median de-rating of five Indian industrial and chemical compounders (SRF, Pidilite, Solar Industries, Navin Fluorine, 3M India) against their five-year median P/E by 30-Sep-2026 (about 86x). No further growth adjustment: our FY26-29E underlying EPS growth (~4% a year) is close to the near-flat EPS the stock delivered while it traded at 114x. Bull 115x (its own median, no de-rating); bear 42x (Ellenbarrie's trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026, the only other listed Indian gas company).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check that counts net debt. 34x Sep-28E EBITDA = Linde India's ~56x median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021, less the same ~25% de-rating (about 42x trailing), restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being ~25% above the twelve months to Jun-2026 excluding the Rs 90 cr reversal (about 34x). Bull 45x, bear 22x.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, cost of equity 11.6%, terminal growth 6%, less net debt.

cover.headline: Good plants, contested governance, and a price that already assumes decades of growth: we initiate at SELL
cover.lead: Linde India is 75% owned by Linde plc, the world's largest industrial-gas company. It sells oxygen, nitrogen and argon from plants inside steel and refinery customers, as merchant liquid and in cylinders (84% of FY26 revenue), and builds air separation plants (Project Engineering). It is spending heavily on four large new plants for Tata Steel, SAIL and Electrosteel, and has a ~₹2,000 cr third-party engineering order book. But profits have barely grown since FY24, ROE is heading to ~10%, and minority shareholders are fighting the parent over business handed to Linde plc's 100%-owned Praxair India. At ₹6,323 the stock trades at 116.4x our FY28E EPS. Coverage is thin and no broker method is public; the Indian street values gas companies on **P/E**. Applying **85x** (its 114.5x forward median since 2021, cut for the ~25% de-rating of quality Indian industrial stocks) **to Sep-28E EPS of ₹56.5** gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with SELL**. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}; our DCF is only ₹668.

arguments.h: The price assumes decades of compounding
arguments.p: 116.4x FY28E EPS and ~55x FY28E EV/EBITDA, against ~25x for Linde plc and 41.6x trailing for Ellenbarrie, the only other listed Indian gas company. A DCF at an 11.6% cost of equity and 6% terminal growth is worth ₹668 a share: even fifteen years of 7-8% revenue growth cannot fill the gap.

arguments.h: Growth is coming, but reaches profit slowly
arguments.p: Gases grew 9.0% in Q1FY27 and PED external revenue doubled. New plants add depreciation and interest first: we forecast EPS of ₹50.4 in FY27E (FY26 ₹64.4 included ~₹12 a share of one-offs), ₹54.3 in FY28E and ₹58.8 in FY29E, with ROE near 10%.

Since 2020 new merchant business in South and Central India, and all hydrogen and CO2 business, goes to Praxair India, which Linde plc owns 100% (FY25 turnover ₹2,771 cr). SEBI and SAT ruled against the company; 89.2% of votes at the Mar-2026 EGM rejected its Praxair dealings; the auditor qualified the FY26 accounts.

A corporate action by Linde plc (delisting, or merging Praxair India into Linde India) would be priced well above fundamentals: in 2019 minorities set a ₹2,025 delisting price against a ₹428.5 floor. The scarcity premium has also lasted for years. Our bull case ({{scen.bull.tp|inr}}) assumes the stock keeps its own median multiple and the plants start on time.

sections.title: What Linde India does: gases from plants inside customers' fences, liquid by tanker, and a plant-building arm

blocks.p: Linde India separates air into oxygen, nitrogen and argon, and sells them three ways. **On-site:** it builds and runs an air separation unit (ASU) inside a large customer's works, often a steel plant (Tata Steel at Jamshedpur and Kalinganagar, SAIL Rourkela, Jindal Stainless at Jajpur) or a refinery (IOCL Panipat), and is paid a fixed monthly facility fee plus a variable charge, with power passed through, for 15-20 years. **Merchant (bulk):** surplus liquid from those plants and from stand-alone merchant ASUs (Selaqui, Ludhiana, Dahej, Taloja) goes by cryogenic tanker to hospitals, glass, electronics, food and metal fabricators; deliveries rose 12% to 2,360 tonnes a day in FY26. **Packaged:** cylinders of industrial, medical and special gases (argon mixes, nitrous oxide, silane). The **Project Engineering Division (PED)** designs and builds ASUs and nitrogen plants for Linde India itself and for outside customers.

sections.title: Industry: regional, capital-heavy and power-hungry; steel and electronics drive demand

blocks.p: Industrial gases are a local business: liquid oxygen or nitrogen cannot travel economically much beyond 200-300 km by road, so returns depend on having plants and customers close together. Power is the main cost (Linde India's power and fuel bill was ₹415 cr in FY26, 16% of revenue). Big users, above all steel makers, either run their own captive ASUs or contract a gas company to build one on-site; Indian steel makers are now selling or outsourcing their captive plants ("de-captivation"), as Tata Steel did at Kalinganagar. The main competitors are INOX Air Products and Praxair India (both unlisted), Air Liquide India, Air Water India and smaller regional players such as Ellenbarrie Industrial Gases (listed Jul-2025, FY26 revenue ₹342 cr). We found no audited market-share data; a widely quoted trade estimate could not be verified.

sections.title: Linde plc owns 75% of Linde India and 100% of Praxair India, a sister company of the same size: that is the core governance problem

blocks.p: The BOC Group (UK), part of Linde plc, owns 75.00% of Linde India, with nothing pledged. When Linde AG and Praxair merged in 2018, Linde plc also acquired Praxair India Pvt Ltd, which it owns 100% and which is about the same size as Linde India: FY25 turnover ₹2,771 cr, profit ₹457 cr, net worth ₹3,957 cr (Linde India FY25: ₹2,485 cr, ₹455 cr, ~₹3,780 cr). On 24-Mar-2020 the two companies signed a JV agreement: a 50:50 services company (LSAS) that provides procurement, safety, HR, finance, IT, legal, sales and plant-management services to both, and a protocol for dividing future business. The protocol: new merchant business allocated by incumbency, else geography: Linde India takes East, North and West India (excluding industrial bulk in Maharashtra); Praxair India takes South and Central India and Maharashtra industrial bulk. Project engineering exclusively with Linde India; CO2, HyCO (hydrogen/carbon monoxide) and PST exclusively with Praxair India. New on-site business allocated on incumbency/technology/competitiveness; expansions and renewals stay with the incumbent.

bullets: **The votes.** In June 2021, 93.94% of votes cast rejected an omnibus approval for dealings with Praxair India and LSAS. The company then treated each contract separately so that none crossed the 10%-of-turnover threshold for a vote; SEBI (Jul-2024) and SAT (Dec-2025) said all dealings with one party must be added up. At an EGM on 5-Mar-2026 the company asked for a ₹417.7 cr FY26 limit; 89.24% of votes cast were against (the promoter could not vote), and it stopped trading with Praxair India for the rest of the year.

**The company's case.** Dealings are at arm's length (an annual EY certificate), margins on Praxair sales exceed 30%, and sourcing from the nearer group plant saves freight; the allocation is "transparent and equitable". It expects to win in the Supreme Court and says the impact of the valuer's report cannot be estimated.

**The open question.** The NSE-appointed valuer reported (16-Mar-2026) on business "allegedly foregone" and "allegedly gained"; the numbers have not been disclosed. SEBI said it will decide further action, including on directors and officers, after the valuation.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is the single most important fact about the stock. A parent that owns 100% of one company and 75% of another has a reason to put growth in the first. The allocation is not obviously unfair (Linde India keeps the steel-heavy East, its engineering monopoly within the group and its incumbent customers), but minorities were not asked and were not compensated, and every regulator so far has agreed with them. Possible outcomes range from compensation to Linde India (positive) to a merger of the two companies or a delisting offer (positive for the price) to years of litigation and restricted dealings (negative). We do not put a value on any of them.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Linde India has a **narrow-to-moderate moat**. Long on-site contracts and dense plant clusters in the East and North are real advantages that rivals cannot copy quickly, and Linde plc's technology helps. But it has no cost edge, merchant pricing is cyclical, and its parent has given the South, Central India, hydrogen and CO2 to a sister company. A narrow moat deserves a premium to the market, not four times Linde plc's multiple.

sections.title: Flat revenue since FY24, higher margins, and a FY26 profit flattered by one-offs

blocks.p: Linde India's revenue was ₹2,769 cr in FY24, ₹2,485 cr in FY25 and ₹2,531 cr in FY26 (FY23 was a 15-month year, so it looks bigger). The FY25 fall was all Project Engineering, whose external revenue dropped from ₹768 cr to ₹445 cr; Gases grew only 2% and 4% a year, partly because on-site power costs, which are passed through to customers, fell. Margins rose a lot: EBITDA margin was 25% in FY24, 31% in FY25 and 36% in FY26, as merchant liquid gas sold well and fewer low-margin projects went through the P&L. But FY26 profit of ₹549 cr (+21%) includes a ₹90 cr reversal of liabilities and a ~₹49 cr one-off from a joint venture being wound up; without them profit was ~₹444 cr, roughly the ₹449 cr of FY25 before exceptional items.

sections.title: Capital allocation: ₹2,100 cr into new plants in two years, a flat ₹12 dividend, and returns heading below the cost of capital

blocks.p: Gross block including work in progress rose from ₹3,757 cr at Mar-2024 to ₹5,322 cr at Mar-2026 (+42%), while EBITDA excluding one-offs rose from ₹702 cr (FY24) to ~₹819 cr (FY26, +17%). New on-site plants take 18-30 months to build and earn their fixed fees only once commissioned, so returns dip before they recover. The dividend has been ₹12 a share (₹102 cr) for four years, including a special dividend each year: 19-23% of profit, the rest reinvested. ROE (Screener basis) was 12.5% in FY24-25 and 13.6% in FY26, against our 11.6% cost of equity; on our numbers it falls to ~10% in FY27-29E.

blocks.callout: **So what:** management is reinvesting ~80% of profit at returns that are, for now, below the cost of equity. That is normal early in a plant cycle, and on-site contracts make the eventual returns fairly predictable, but the company does not disclose project costs or expected returns, so shareholders are asked to take them on trust.

sections.title: Earnings quality: real cash, but a qualified audit opinion and one-offs in FY26

bullets: **One-offs in FY26.** Expenses were reduced by a ₹90 cr "reversal of related liabilities considering change in certain contractual arrangements" (Q2FY26, Gases segment; no further explanation given), and the consolidated P&L includes ~₹49 cr from the Bellary Oxygen JV, which sold its plant to JSW Steel and is being wound up. Together ~₹105 cr after tax, a fifth of FY26 profit.

**Qualified audit opinion.** PwC qualified the FY26 standalone and consolidated statements: the effect of applying SEBI's aggregate test to related-party dealings is "presently not determinable". It also added an emphasis of matter on the SEBI-ordered valuation. The Q1FY27 limited review carries the same qualification.

**Engineering revenue is an estimate.** PED revenue is booked on percentage of completion; cost-to-complete is a key audit matter. Plants built for Linde India itself are eliminated "at cost", which supports reported external PED margins.
**Costs capitalised.** ₹8.5 cr of retainer and other costs were capitalised into projects in FY26 (₹8.1 cr in FY25); small, but it rises with the capex programme.
**Lease accounting.** On-site plants dedicated to one customer are treated as operating leases (Linde India as lessor): ₹127 cr of lease rentals in FY26.

**Cash conversion is good.** Operating cash flow was ₹786 cr in FY26 against net profit of ₹549 cr; cash from operations has been 82-121% of EBITDA (before tax) every year since CY18. Customer advances (₹377 cr) and long supplier credit fund working capital.
**Contingent liabilities are small:** ₹75 cr (excise, sales tax, income tax), against ₹4,266 cr of net worth.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Profits turn into cash and the P&L is simple. The amber is for the qualified opinion (a compliance matter whose financial effect is unknown), a fifth of FY26 profit coming from one-offs that were thinly explained, and engineering revenue that rests on estimates.

sections.title: From ₹980 cr of cash to borrowing again: two years of heavy capex used up the cash pile

blocks.p: After selling its South Region business to Air Water India in 2019 (₹1,380 cr) and repaying all debt, Linde India built up cash: ₹980 cr at Mar-2024. Then the capex cycle started: cash capex was ₹572 cr in FY24, ₹1,331 cr in FY25 and ₹766 cr in FY26, against operating cash flow of ₹437 cr, ₹584 cr and ₹786 cr. Cash fell to ₹147 cr (Mar-2025) and ₹112 cr (Mar-2026); capital work in progress rose to ₹1,343 cr, and ₹755 cr of advances had been paid for plants still to be delivered (capital commitments ₹695 cr on top). The company had no bank debt at Mar-2026, only ₹79 cr of lease liabilities. In Q1FY27 finance cost doubled from the March quarter and unallocated liabilities rose by ~₹568 cr; the company did not say why, but borrowing to fund capex is the likely reason.

sections.title: Our forecasts: EPS resets in FY27, then grows ~8% a year as the new plants start

blocks.p: We model the two reported segments separately. Gases grow 11% / 12% / 10% in FY27-29E as the JSL, second Tata Kalinganagar, Dahej, SAIL Rourkela and Electrosteel plants come on stream, with segment EBITDA margin rising from FY26's underlying 36.3% to 36.5%. Project Engineering external revenue rises sharply in FY27E on the semiconductor and refinery orders and margins return towards the long-run ~15%. Unallocated corporate costs grow ~6% a year. Depreciation rises with the new plants (6.6% of gross block), interest rises as capex is funded partly with debt, tax is 25.5% and the dividend stays ~₹12-13 a share. FY27E EPS falls 22% because FY26 included ~₹12 a share of one-offs; on an underlying basis (FY26 ~₹52.1) it falls ~3%. sections.title: The street: almost no public coverage, and the little there is cannot be verified

blocks.p: Coverage is thin and not public. We found no broker note on Linde India with a disclosed rating, target, method and earnings year dated Jul-Sep 2026. A blog updated on 16-Jun-2026 lists JM Financial (Neutral, ₹7,800) and Kotak Securities (Neutral, ₹7,300) without dates, methods or links; we could not verify either. We found no estimates of FY27-29E EPS. The plain conclusion: for a ₹54,000 cr company, Linde India is barely covered, and the price is set by a small float rather than by analysts. sections.title: Our honest summary: a business worth owning at the right price, and this is not it

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's leading listed industrial-gas company, owned and run by the global leader; long take-or-pay contracts with Tata Steel, SAIL, JSL and IOCL; dense plant clusters in the East and North; four large plants under construction; a ~₹2,000 cr third-party engineering order book; almost no debt today.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Linde India (consolidated, Rs crore). Segment model on the two reported segments: Gases & related products (external revenue = segment revenue) and Project Engineering on EXTERNAL revenue only (PED segment revenue less inter-segment plants built for Gases, which are eliminated at cost), so the two sum to reported revenue. Segment margin = segment EBITDA (segment result + segment D&A, AR note 42) as % of segment revenue. Unallocated corporate costs (Screener EBITDA less the sum of segment EBITDA) are a separate line. Treasury income = yield x opening net cash (zero when net debt); other income = recurring non-treasury income plus the LSAS JV share. Valued on P/E, the method the Indian street uses for listed industrial-gas companies.

segments.name: Gases & related products
segments._why: FY26 +4.3% (merchant deliveries +12% to 2,360 TPD; on-site power pass-through fell ~Rs 106 cr, depressing reported revenue). Q1FY27 +9.0%. FY27 +11%: full year of the JSL Jajpur 1,450 tpd ASU and IOCL Panipat N2 plant (capitalised in FY26), the second Tata Steel Kalinganagar 1,800 TPD ASU and the third Dahej ASU (commissioning FY27), merchant growth ~8-10%. FY28 +12%: SAIL Rourkela 1,000 TPD and Electrosteel Bokaro 900 TPD ASUs (under construction at Aug-2026) ramp up. FY29 +10%: steel 6-8% and electronics/solar 18-20% end-market growth (company view) with no new large plant assumed.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 33.7% (FY24), 35.8% (FY25), 40.6% (FY26 incl. the Rs 90 cr reversal; 36.3% without it). Q4FY26 ~36% and Q1FY27 ~35% (PBIT margin 24.3% vs 25.8%: power tariffs, overheads, new-plant depreciation). New on-site plants carry fixed facility fees, so margin rises gently: 35.5% / 36% / 36.5%.

segments.name: Project Engineering (external)
segments._why: External PED revenue: Rs 768 cr (FY24), Rs 445 cr (FY25), Rs 402 cr (FY26); Q1FY27 Rs 150 cr (2.1x Q1FY26). Third-party order book ~Rs 2,000 cr (AGM, Aug-2026) incl. Tata Electronics' Dholera fab and Assam OSAT, Reliance Nagothane ASU, Adani and PSU nitrogen plants. FY27 ~Rs 644 cr (+60%), FY28 ~Rs 740 cr, FY29 ~Rs 703 cr as the current order book is executed; lumpy.
segments._marginWhy: PED PBIT margin on external revenue was 11-14% in CY18-FY24, then 22% (FY25) and 30% (FY26) when inter-segment work for the company's own plants was large (Rs 661 cr and Rs 578 cr) and absorbed overheads; Q1FY27 ~16% EBITDA as external work rose and inter-segment work fell to Rs 75 cr. We assume 16% / 15% / 15%, nearer the long-run level.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Unallocated corporate costs (sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA)
assumptions._unallocWhy: Rs 77 cr (FY24), Rs 70 cr (FY25), Rs 78 cr (FY26): head-office, governance, legal (SEBI/SAT/Supreme Court) and other costs not allocated to segments. Grows ~6% a year.
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex Rs 572 cr (FY24), Rs 1,331 cr (FY25), Rs 766 cr (FY26). At Mar-2026: CWIP Rs 1,343 cr, capital commitments Rs 695 cr net of Rs 755 cr of advances already paid. Projects under construction: Tata Kalinganagar second 1,800 TPD ASU, SAIL Rourkela 1,000 TPD, Electrosteel Bokaro 900 TPD, Dahej third ASU, ammonia purification (Gujarat). No guidance; we assume Rs 900 / 750 / 650 cr incl. ~Rs 150 cr a year of maintenance, cylinders and logistics (FY26: Rs 37 cr on special-gas trailers alone).
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs 235 cr = 6.2% of average gross block (Rs 3,780 cr). Q1FY27 Rs 62 cr (Rs 250 cr annualised). The engine holds CWIP (Rs 1,343 cr) flat and depreciates capex at once, so we use 6.6% to capture CWIP being capitalised as the Tata, SAIL and Dahej plants start.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied only to positive opening net cash (cash Rs 112 cr + Rs 82 cr investments in renewable SPVs less Rs 79 cr lease liabilities at Mar-2026); with capex above operating cash flow, net cash turns to net debt and this line falls to zero.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Recurring non-treasury other income and the LSAS JV share: FY26 consolidated other income Rs 18 cr plus normal JV share ~Rs 7 cr (excluding the ~Rs 49 cr Bellary Oxygen one-off); Q1FY27 Rs 5.8 cr + Rs 1.6 cr.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest cost (leases and borrowings to fund capex)
assumptions._interestWhy: Rs 13 cr (FY25), Rs 14.5 cr (FY26, incl. Rs 6.2 cr on leases); Q1FY27 Rs 5.9 cr (double Q4FY26). Lease liabilities rose to Rs 79 cr. Capex above operating cash flow after dividends means borrowings of roughly Rs 500-700 cr by FY28 at ~7.5-8%, plus leases.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 consolidated 25.2% (Rs 184.5 cr on Rs 733.5 cr PBT); Q1FY27 25.1%; new regime 25.17% plus deferred tax on the JV.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend held at Rs 12 a share (Rs 102 cr, incl. a special) for FY23-FY26: 19-23% of EPS. We keep roughly Rs 12-13 a share.

dcf._betaWhy: Long-term take-or-pay contracts and a parent-backed balance sheet make cash flows steadier than the market, but merchant pricing, steel and project lumpiness add cyclicality: beta 0.85, cost of equity 11.6%. The engine discounts at the cost of equity; with little debt this is close to WACC.
dcf._tgWhy: Industrial gases grow with industrial output and nominal GDP; 6% nominal, the top of the house 5-6% range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% to 8% by year 15 (India nominal GDP ~10%; gases ~1x industrial growth).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin fades from ~32% to 32%: gases mix rises but power costs and competition cap it; Linde plc's group EBITDA margin is ~38-40% at global scale.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Gases are capital-heavy (gross block incl. CWIP ~2x sales); growing ~8% needs capex of ~14% of sales (Linde plc spends ~16% of sales).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: All four large ASUs start on time and merchant liquid stays tight: gases grow ~14% a year with EBITDA margin near 38%; PED executes the semiconductor and refinery orders faster at ~18%; the Supreme Court sides with the company and the Praxair matter fades.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Steel capex slows and project start-ups slip a year; INOX, Air Liquide and Air Water add merchant capacity and liquid prices fall; gases grow ~8% with margin ~33.5%; PED orders are delayed and margins fall to ~12%; SEBI acts on the valuation report.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: No broker method for Linde India is public; the Indian street values listed industrial-gas companies on one-year-forward P/E (Motilal Oswal initiated Ellenbarrie at 40x FY27E EPS in Sep-2025). 85x Sep-28E EPS = the stock's 114.5x median one-year-forward P/E since Apr-2021 (forwardMedian; the Apr-2021 to Mar-2022 points drop out because FY23 was a 15-month year; no trough years), cut by the ~25% median de-rating of five Indian industrial and chemical compounders (SRF, Pidilite, Solar Industries, Navin Fluorine, 3M India) against their five-year median P/E by 30-Sep-2026 (about 86x). No further growth adjustment: our FY26-29E underlying EPS growth (~4% a year) is close to the near-flat EPS the stock delivered while it traded at 114x. Bull 115x (its own median, no de-rating); bear 42x (Ellenbarrie's trailing P/E on 30-Sep-2026, the only other listed Indian gas company).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check that counts net debt. 34x Sep-28E EBITDA = Linde India's ~56x median trailing EV/EBITDA since Apr-2021, less the same ~25% de-rating (about 42x trailing), restated for Sep-28E EBITDA being ~25% above the twelve months to Jun-2026 excluding the Rs 90 cr reversal (about 34x). Bull 45x, bear 22x.
